<reason>B won the burden-for-irreversible-release clash. A never solved the gap where tests are complete but a credible dangerous adaptation remains untested, and A's answer that plausible tests must be run first conceded B's point that absence of a crossed threshold is not enough for permission. B also neutralized delay/concentration with deadlines, subsidies, and accountable access, while A's copyability and defender-advantage points were reduced to degree not kind.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2 turn on A's concession: if unfinished plausible tests can withhold release without a crossed threshold, PRO needs a substantive safety judgment, not just a threshold, plus the reply that cutting hosting cannot constrain already-downloaded offline weights.</best_rebuttal>
